    🦇 Demonism¶

    "Day belongs to those who take. Night belongs to those who endure."

    Demonism is the faith of the Diablos — winged, nocturnal humanoids of the Mountain Tribe on Yak Island east of the Demon Continent mainland. Where most demon faiths are variations of Kirivs-bin, Demonism is the sharpest break: it worships demon-ness itself as a night-vocation — to be the winged watchers who keep the world honest while the day-species sleep.

    The name Demonism is a reclaimed slander. Erisdar missionaries once called the Diablos "demons of the night" as an insult; the Diablos kept the word and made it a title.

    Origins¶

    Diablos are strictly nocturnal — sleeping through daylight in cliff-face settlements accessible only by flight, convening their Night Council only after moonrise. For millennia they had no theology beyond moon-tracking (births, marriages, wars timed to lunar conjunctions) and a quiet pride in endurance.

    Demonism crystallized after sustained contact with the Asatru Empire's Knight's Thorn garrisons and Estran traders, who brought tales of Kirivis and called the Diablos "not truly demonic." The Diablos' answer, codified around ~400 BGD by Night Council elder Shara Half-Moon, was to claim the word more fiercely than their critics used it: if demon means one who tests, endures, and watches in darkness, then Diablos are the truest demons on Ge'or.

    Shara's Moon Letters — twelve short admonitions copied onto night-silk — remain the faith's only quasi-scripture.

    Beliefs¶

    • Night is not the absence of day — it is its judge — Demonism teaches that daylight is for claiming, building, and taking; night is for accounting. The Diablos' vocation is to remain awake while others sleep and to remember what daylight forgets.
    • Flight is witness — wings are not transport but testimony. A winged being who can see the island entire from above and says nothing is complicit; a winged being who sees and later speaks at the Night Council has done holy work.
    • The moon is clock, not god — Diablos track Maenar and Amelia with religious precision, but they do not worship the moons. The moons are the impartial timekeepers who prove that a promise made at waxing can be measured at waning. Demonism is lunar-accurate but not lunar-devotional — a distinction Moongar cults never grasp.
    • Sunlight wounds, but does not refute — direct sun causes Diablos physical discomfort and skin damage on prolonged exposure. Demonism reads this not as curse but as calling: they are shaped for the watch others cannot keep.
    • Kirivis as night-revealer — Demonist readings of Kirivs-bin foreground Kirivis's act of seeing what no one else would see — in Demonist shorthand, "the demon who stayed awake." They remain within the bin communion while insisting the bin has forgotten its own night-side.

    Practices¶

    • Night Council liturgy — governance and worship are the same act. The council convenes only after moonrise; no decision is valid if made in daylight. Proceedings open with a wing-silence (all present extend wings and hold still until the wind is the only sound) and close with a recitation of Shara's twelve letters.
    • Moon-silver and shadow-silk offering — Diablos trade moon-silver ore and shadow-silk (spun from cave-dwelling moths) and night-blooming herbs. The first ingot of a new vein and the first bolt of a silk season are not sold but hung on the cliff-face as night-decor — visible only to those who fly after dark.
    • Thermal gliding prayer — sustained flight is prayer when flown without cargo or errand — purely to patrol, observe, and later report. A Diablos who flies an empty circuit of Yak Island and returns with "nothing to report" is praised for confirming stillness.
    • Nocturnal hospitality — Diablos maintain intermediary outposts lit only by moon-silver lanterns where Estran and Asatru traders can meet them at dusk or dawn. To force a Diablos to meet at noon is an insult in Demonist terms; to meet them at midnight is to honor their vocation.
    • Sound-dampening chant — Diablos mages specialize in shadow and sound-dampening magic; their low, layered humming before a Night Council session is both practical (hushing echoes in the cliff halls) and sacramental.

    Relation to Kirivs-bin and Other Faiths¶

    Demonism claims Kirivs-bin lineage while refusing to be a mere sect. Asatru theologians classify it as "the nocturnal bin" — a legitimate but willfully contrarian branch. Demonists accept the classification the way they accepted the name: with a thin smile that does not confirm anything.

    Relations are:

    • Warmest with Estran (High Catmen) — whose elective cunning and night-savvy trading complements Diablo patrol rhythms
    • Respectful but strained with Asatru — which admires Diablo discipline while finding their refusal to normalize daylight commerce inconvenient
    • Indifferent to Erisdar missionary faiths — Demonism considers solar triumphalism a category error

    There is no Demonist priesthood beyond the Night Council elders; no temple beyond the cliff-face itself. In that austerity Demonism is truer to Kirivs-bin than many Asatru think.

    Influence¶

    • Majority: Mountain Tribe — universal among Diablos; faith, governance, and daily schedule are one thing
    • Minority: small Diablos enclaves and night-workers in Asatru-controlled territory on Yak Island and the Demon mainland foothills
    • Viewed across the Demon Continent as the "demons who mean it" — Asatru soldiers joke that you can set your watch by a Diablos patrol, and that the joke is theology
    • The faith's island isolation means it rarely proselytizes; those who want to understand it must be willing to stay up all night

    Connections¶
